Basilica of San Petronio

The must-sees

7 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Culture · 1563

    Archiginnasio

    Built in 1563, it was the first single seat of the university. Its wooden Anatomical Theatre was destroyed by bombing in 1944 and rebuilt from the original pieces.

    Look for

    In the Anatomical Theatre, two wooden skinned men, the Spellati, hold up the canopy over the lecturer’s chair.

  2. 02
    Church

    Basilica of San Petronio

    Building began in 1390 and the façade was never finished. A long meridian line set into the floor by the astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini in the 1650s still marks noon with a beam of sunlight.

    Look for

    Around the central door, Jacopo della Quercia’s stone reliefs tell Genesis, from the creation of Adam to Noah.

  3. 03
    Landmark

    Fountain of Neptune

    Giambologna made the bronze figures in the 1560s for a papal project to beautify the city. Locals call the statue simply il Gigante, the Giant.

    Look for

    On the town hall wall facing the fountain, rows of photographs remember the partisans of Bologna killed in the Second World War.

  4. 04
    Square

    Piazza Maggiore

    It has been the centre of city life since the Middle Ages. In summer it becomes an open-air cinema in front of San Petronio.

    Look for

    Under the vault beneath Palazzo del Podestà, two people whispering into opposite corners can hear each other clearly across the space.

  5. 05
    Church

    Sanctuary of San Luca

    The portico has 666 arches, built with money from the city’s families and guilds. Every year an image of the Madonna is carried down to the cathedral and back.

    Look for

    Where the portico leaves the plain and starts to climb, it crosses the road on the Meloncello arch, a curved Baroque bridge.

  6. 06
    Church

    Santo Stefano

    Known as the Seven Churches, the complex grew over many centuries around a round church modelled on the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. The cloister and courtyards connect them.

    Look for

    In the open courtyard, find the large stone basin called Pilate’s Basin. It is an 8th-century Lombard piece, linked to Pilate only by legend.

  7. 07
    Landmark

    Two Towers

    Rich families built dozens of towers in medieval Bologna, and these two from the 12th century are the best known. The Asinelli is close to 100 metres tall; the shorter Garisenda leans hard.

    Look for

    Look up at the Garisenda from the street and follow its lean. It was cut down in the 14th century because it tilted so far.
